# kafka-collector

> Record Kafka messages as JSON Lines. One process, one consumer, two modes: `cli` streams records to stdout or a file; `service` writes rolling capture files and exposes three HTTP endpoints to finalize, list, and download them.

Collect only. This tool does not create topics, produce messages, or read topic history. It is step 1 of collect → convert ([collector-to-emulator](https://github.com/siakhooi/collector-to-emulator)) → replay ([kafka-emulator](https://github.com/siakhooi/kafka-emulator)).

Package `kafka_collector` (pip). Command `kafka-collector`. Python >= 3.10. Image `siakhooi/kafka-collector` with entrypoint `kafka-collector` (flags or env, same as the CLI).

## Install and run

```bash
pip install kafka_collector
kafka-collector -t orders,payments -b localhost:9092
kafka-collector -m service -t orders,payments -b localhost:9092 -p 8080
```

Docker passes the same flags after the image name, or uses the environment variables below:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 \
  -e KAFKA_TOPICS=orders \
  -e KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVER=kafka:9092 \
  -e COLLECTOR_MODE=service \
  -e COLLECTOR_CAPTURE_DIR=/data/captures \
  siakhooi/kafka-collector:latest
```

The process runs until SIGINT or SIGTERM. Argument and fatal errors print `Error: …` on stderr and exit 1. Logs go to stderr, so CLI stdout stays a pure JSONL stream.

## Configuration

A passed flag wins. Otherwise the environment variable is used. An unset flag and an empty variable both fall through to the default. Topics have no default.

| Setting | Flag | Environment | Default | Applies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Topics | `-t`, `--topics` | `KAFKA_TOPICS` | required | both |
| Bootstrap server | `-b`, `--bootstrap-server` | `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` | `localhost:9092` | both |
| Consumer group | `-g`, `--group` | `KAFKA_GROUP` | new UUID every process | both |
| Mode | `-m`, `--mode` | `COLLECTOR_MODE` | `cli` | both |
| Output path | `-o`, `--output` | none | `-` (stdout) | cli |
| Capture directory | `-c`, `--capture-dir` | `COLLECTOR_CAPTURE_DIR` | `/tmp/kafka-collector` | service |
| HTTP port | `-p`, `--port` | `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_PORT` | `8080` | service |
| Log level | `--log-level` | `LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | both |
| Debug | `--debug` | none | off | both |

`--debug` forces `DEBUG` and outranks both `--log-level` and `LOG_LEVEL`.

Topics are a comma-separated list. Surrounding whitespace is stripped and empty entries are dropped. At least one topic is required. A topic name cannot contain a comma.

Mode is `cli` or `service`. Port must be an integer. Log level is `debug`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, or `critical` (any case). An invalid `LOG_LEVEL` prints a warning and the process continues at `INFO`.

Mismatched flags warn on stderr and are ignored: `-o` in service mode; `-c` and `-p` in CLI mode.

Service mode creates the capture directory. Failure to create it exits 1. The default `/tmp/kafka-collector` is for local use; point `-c` or `COLLECTOR_CAPTURE_DIR` at a private path when other users can write `/tmp`.

`kafka` and `werkzeug` loggers stay at WARNING. Application logs use `kafka_collector` and the format `time - logger - LEVEL - message`.

## What the consumer does

On startup the process subscribes to every topic in the list, polls until partitions are assigned, then reads.

`auto_offset_reset` is `latest` and auto-commit is on. For a consumer group that already has committed offsets, consumption resumes at those offsets. For a new group (the default UUID, or a group that has never committed), consumption starts at the end. Messages published before assignment are not collected. There is no flag to rewind to the beginning.

Set `-g` / `KAFKA_GROUP` when a restart should continue the same group. Leave the group unset when each run should see only messages that arrive after it connects.

Wait until stderr shows `Consumer connected and assigned partitions` before producing the messages you intend to capture.

Keys and values must be UTF-8 text or null. A non-UTF-8 key or value stops the process. Header values are copied from the client record; binary headers are not JSON-serializable and also stop the process. Captures of header-less text records are the supported case.

## Record format

One JSON object per line:

```json
{"topic":"orders","timestamp":1711900800000,"header":{},"value":"payload","key":"k1"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `topic` | Topic name |
| `timestamp` | Kafka record timestamp, milliseconds |
| `header` | Header map, `{}` when the record has none |
| `value` | UTF-8 payload, or `null` |
| `key` | UTF-8 key, or `null` |

Every topic shares one stream. Select on `topic`.

## CLI mode

Default mode. Each record is written as one line and flushed immediately.

```bash
kafka-collector -t orders,payments -b kafka:9092
kafka-collector -t orders -o /var/log/orders.jsonl
kafka-collector -t orders | jq -c 'select(.topic=="orders")'
```

`-o -` is stdout. Any other `-o` path is opened in append mode and must already have a parent directory. A later run with the same path adds lines; it does not replace the file.

```bash
export KAFKA_TOPICS=orders,payments
export KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVER=kafka:9092
export KAFKA_GROUP=collector-dev
kafka-collector -o ./orders.jsonl
```

## Service mode

HTTP server on `0.0.0.0:$port` (Flask’s built-in server, no authentication). Keep it on a private network. A background thread appends the same JSONL records to the open capture file and flushes each line.

```bash
kafka-collector -m service -t orders,payments -b kafka:9092 \
  -c /data/captures -p 8080 -g collector-dev
```

Files on disk are named `kafka-collector_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_ffffff.jsonl` (UTC). The open file is not listed and not downloadable. `POST /reset` closes it, registers it under a name, and opens the next file. The name index lives in process memory: a restart leaves the JSONL files in the capture directory and clears the index, so the API will not list or serve captures from a previous process.

### POST /reset

Finalize the open capture and start a new one. Body is optional JSON.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/reset \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"morning-batch"}'
```

`200`:

```json
{"status":"ok","new_file":"/data/captures/kafka-collector_20240331_120000_123456.jsonl"}
```

`new_file` is the capture that starts receiving messages after this call, not the file just closed. The closed file is available under `name`.

Omit `name`, or send `{}`, and the server assigns an 8-character hex id. A provided name is stripped and must be 1–256 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_`, `.`, `-`, and unique among captures completed in this process.

`400` body is `{"error":"<message>"}`:

| Message | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `name must not be empty` | blank name |
| `name exceeds maximum length (256)` | name too long |
| `name contains invalid characters` | character outside the set above |
| `name '<name>' already exists` | name reused in this process |

### GET /files

Completed captures only, oldest first. `200` with `[]` before the first reset. This is the liveness check (the image healthcheck calls it). `GET /` is not a route.

```json
[
  {
    "name": "morning-batch",
    "path": "/data/captures/kafka-collector_20240331_120000_123456.jsonl",
    "completed_at": "2024-03-31T12:00:00.123456+00:00"
  }
]
```

`path` is the server’s filesystem path.

### GET /download

Download one completed capture.

| Query | Required | Default | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | no | last completed | capture name |
| `type` | no | `jsonl` | `jsonl` or `zip` |

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/download -o capture.jsonl
curl -sS 'http://localhost:8080/download?name=morning-batch' -o morning-batch.jsonl
curl -sS 'http://localhost:8080/download?name=morning-batch&type=zip' -o morning-batch.zip
```

`type=jsonl` returns `application/jsonl` and the on-disk basename (`kafka-collector_….jsonl`). `type=zip` returns `application/zip` as `<name>.zip` containing that basename.

| Status | Message |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `no completed files` |
| 400 | `duplicate name parameter` or `duplicate type parameter` |
| 400 | `type must be jsonl or zip` |
| 400 | same name errors as `/reset`, when `name` is present but invalid |
| 404 | `name '<name>' not found` |
| 404 | `capture file is missing or inaccessible` |

Call `POST /reset` before download. Download reads only completed captures. Stop the process only after the reset you intend to keep; the still-open file is closed on shutdown and is not added to the index.

### Capture sequence

```bash
kafka-collector -m service -t orders -b localhost:9092 -p 8080
# wait for "Consumer connected and assigned partitions", then produce
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/reset -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"run1"}'
curl -s localhost:8080/files
curl -sS 'localhost:8080/download?name=run1' -o run1.jsonl
```

## Deployed examples

`docker-compose/` runs Kafka (KRaft) and the collector in service mode. The compose network is external: `docker network create kafka-collector` before `docker compose up`. Collector settings in that file: topics `topic1,topic2`, bootstrap `kafka:9092`, group `my-consumer-group`, mode `service`, port `8080`, capture dir `/data/captures` mounted from `./captures`. The broker advertises `kafka:9092`, so use that address from containers on this network.

`kubernetes/` is service mode via the `kafka-collector-config` ConfigMap (`envFrom`), a single replica, a ClusterIP Service on port 8080, and an `emptyDir` at `/data/captures`. The emptyDir and the in-memory name index both disappear when the pod restarts. Reach it with `kubectl port-forward svc/kafka-collector 8080:8080`.
